skill.name: wiki-researcher
skill.description: Conducts multi-turn iterative deep research on specific topics within a codebase with zero tolerance for shallow analysis. Use when the user wants an in-depth investigation, needs to understand how something works across multiple files, or asks for comprehensive analysis of a specific system or pattern.
skill.summary: Guides evidence-based codebase research with iterative architecture, data flow, dependency, pattern, and synthesis analysis.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives in Markdown prose, not executable behavior. The first is inline-code formatting for citation syntax, and the second is guidance for diagrams in architecture explanations. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - Include Mermaid diagrams (dark-mode colors) when they clarify architecture or flow

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 61 is a Markdown bullet requiring citations in `(file_path:line_number)` format. The backticks delimit inline text and do not invoke Ruby or shell execution.
Line 63 is an instruction to include Mermaid diagrams when they clarify architecture or flow. It does not request host enumeration, system discovery, or collection of environment details.

content.value_statement: Deep codebase questions are hard to answer without tracing real implementations. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured evidence-based research.
actual_capabilities: Guides five research passes across architecture, data flow, dependencies, patterns, and recommendations.
Requires citations to file paths and line numbers for significant findings.
Separates direct evidence from inference and confidence levels.
Prompts the assistant to trace call chains across multiple files.
Encourages focused Mermaid diagrams when they clarify architecture or flow.
limitations: It provides research guidance, not automated code indexing or static analysis.
Results depend on the assistant reading enough relevant files.
It does not execute tests or verify runtime behavior by itself.
Large repositories may require multiple sessions to cover all important paths.

use_cases.title: Map a Feature
use_cases.description: A developer traces how one feature moves through entry points, services, data stores, and outputs.

use_cases.title: Prepare Architecture Notes
use_cases.description: A technical writer gathers grounded evidence before documenting how a subsystem works.

use_cases.title: Assess Technical Debt
use_cases.description: An engineering lead reviews coupling, anti-patterns, and risks before planning refactoring work.

prompt_templates.title: Understand a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wiki-researcher to explain how [component] works. Trace the real implementation and cite every significant claim.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Data Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wiki-researcher to trace how [data or request] moves from [entry point] to [destination]. Include transformations, dependencies, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Implementations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wiki-researcher to compare how [feature A] and [feature B] are implemented. Identify shared paths, differences, risks, and evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Research Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wiki-researcher to produce a full five-pass analysis of [system]. Cover architecture, state, integrations, patterns, recommendations, confidence, and unanswered questions.

output_examples.input: Explain how user authentication works in this repository.
output_examples.output: Identifies route registration, request handlers, token validation, session storage, and cited confidence levels.

output_examples.input: Trace where pricing data comes from and where it is displayed.
output_examples.output: Shows entry points, service calls, transformations, UI consumers, and open questions for untraced paths.

output_examples.input: Review the notification subsystem for technical debt.
output_examples.output: Lists coupling, repeated patterns, risk areas, and recommended next steps with supporting file references.

best_practices: Start with a narrow topic and expand only when the trace requires it.
Ask for citations and confidence ratings for every important conclusion.
Use follow-up prompts to close open questions after each research pass.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a whole repository summary without a specific system or feature.
Do not accept diagrams that are not tied to verified implementation paths.
Do not treat inferred architecture as fact without cited evidence.

faq.question: What kind of work is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for deep codebase investigations that need evidence, citations, and clear confidence levels.

faq.question: Does it modify code?
faq.answer: No. It is a research and analysis skill. It does not request code edits by itself.

faq.question: Can it analyze large repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, but broad topics may need several focused passes to avoid shallow coverage.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill is written as guidance for reading repository files and tracing implementation details.

faq.question: Can it create diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for Mermaid diagrams only when they clarify verified architecture or flow.

faq.question: How should I phrase a prompt?
faq.answer: Name the feature, subsystem, or data path you want traced, and request cited evidence.
